end.summary:
Ishita practised showing sequence growth by adding a row and column in pictures.
They identified that the shared corner must not be counted twice.
They corrected the 6-by-6 to 7-by-7 growth count to 13 coins.
They used a 3-by-3 picture to explain why 9 is a square number and a picture as evidence for a pattern.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised using dot and tile pictures to show how square patterns grow and why a picture supports a mathematical claim. They explained the shared-corner issue and later corrected the 6-by-6 to 7-by-7 count from 12 to 13. At home, ask them to draw a 4-by-4 square growing to 5-by-5 and label the new row, new column, and shared corner.
